population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: ever 28.8% − current 19.1% = 9.7% of adults have used and are off now. New ever-users since 2030 add 2.3 pts: 1.6 on and 0.7 already off. Of the 18.8 on in 2030, 12.0 stayed on (64% two-year persistence, up from 51%) and 6.8 stopped. Those 6.8 joined the 7.7 already off for a pool of 14.5, of whom 5.5 restarted (38%, down from 55% because the off-pool is now older and more deliberate). So on = 12.0 + 5.5 + 1.6 = 19.1 and off = 9.0 + 0.7 = 9.7. Cycled: 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030, plus ~2.4 pts of first-time restarters, = 11.3 of 28.8 ever-users = 39%. Why persistence rose: the permanent Medicare benefit and Medicaid national rate ended the Bridge-renewal and cessation-cap churn for millions, and MariTide's monthly dosing (late 2031) helps at the margin. Population is ~270M adults, so current users ≈ 51.6M. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23 give 1.9 + 6.4 + 7.3 + 3.5 = 19.1. 65+ rose from 12% to 15% (≈9.3M) under the permanent Medicare benefit. Income thirds average (24.5 + 18 + 14.8)/3 = 19.1. Bottom-third use is up through Medicaid opt-ins. Top-third use dipped slightly as 'focus' subscriptions shrank after the FTC orders and some long-term users stopped over 'the grey'. Off-drug: ~26M adults used and stopped, and ~192M (71%) never used. With normalisation, never-users increasingly have to explain themselves: religious and 'natural-body' communities, people with contraindications, people with eating-disorder histories, and the uninsured in non-opt-in states. Pediatric: 0.7% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 510k, down from ~580k. Of these ≈60k are aged 6–11, down from ~90k after the May 2032 growth signal paused HRSA new starts and the AAP restricted under-12 initiation to pediatric endocrinologists. Children of the 2025–28 adolescent cohort are now young adults with up to 9 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: Public programmes are now the default payer: Medicare + Medicaid + HRSA fund 41.6% of incretin fills, against 30% for all commercial plans combined. Medicare: the December 2031 year-end package converted the GLP-1 Bridge into a permanent Part D obesity benefit from Jan 2032. Criteria are unchanged (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity), the copay stays $50, and the DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+ is kept. The negotiated payment steps down from $275 to $245 (semaglutide), with tirzepatide at $265. Medicare pays 19% of fills ≈ 9.8M users (≈9.2M aged 65+, ≈0.6M disabled under-65). At a blended $250: 9.8M × $250 × 12 ≈ $29.4B/yr across all indications, of which the obesity-only benefit is ≈4.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $13.5B. Medicaid: the CMS National Incretin Rate (Feb 2032) sets net $199/month for states that opt in to obesity coverage; 36 states plus DC have opted in. Medicaid pays 16% ≈ 8.3M users: 8.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $19.8B/yr combined federal and state. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program has a two-year appropriation at $4.8B for FY2032. It serves 3.4M users: 2.0M on generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 = $1.68B, plus 1.4M on semaglutide (cessation, AUD, and uninsured adults in non-opt-in states) × $179 × 12 = $3.01B, plus $0.1B for pediatric growth monitoring, ≈ $4.79B.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month and has approved generic tirzepatide. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China have multi-source generic semaglutide. Generic oral semaglutide is available in ~180 countries. US generic entry for semaglutide is set by patent settlements for 2033, and tirzepatide later.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~51.6M users: Medicare 19% (9.8M), Medicaid 16% (8.3M), HRSA free 6.6% (3.4M), commercial 30% (15.5M), cash/direct 12% (6.2M), gray 16.4% (8.5M) = 100%. Commercial fell from 17.8M to 15.5M as retirees and low-wage workers moved to Medicare and opted-in Medicaid, and as three large employers dropped weight coverage, citing the public option. Managed decline: the July 2031 manufacturer–administration agreement cut TrumpRx/direct cash prices to $249 (semaglutide injection), $299 (tirzepatide) and $149 (oral starting doses, Foundayo and the Wegovy pill). MariTide launched at $1,100 list and $299/month cash. Wegovy list is still $1,349. Retatrutide is still $1,499 list, allocated, with no cash price. Gray-market prices: 503A compounded semaglutide $99–199, Indian mail pens $6–40 plus shipping, research retatrutide $100–220. The narrower gap with branded cash prices trimmed gray use from 9.0M to 8.5M.

indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029; growth-monitoring requirement added 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm/focus' low-dose oral subscriptions, now smaller (~0.9M) after FTC consent orders and sold as 'craving support' without mood claims
'metabolic health' and longevity regimens with DEXA and strength coaching, top income third
planned 'flat-week' dose reductions and holidays, discussed and scheduled with prescribers
gambling and cannabis reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new indication this step (driver: none). Monthly driver: MariTide's BLA was filed Jul 2030 and approved Sep 2031 (14 months) for chronic weight management at ~16–19% mean loss. First-dose vomiting is common and requires slow titration. Clinic administration is offered, and about 1.6M users were on it by end-2032. No implant is on the US market. Survodutide was resubmitted: a split advisory committee in Jun 2032 left its PDUFA date at Jan 2033. Amycretin's resubmission was accepted in Mar 2032 after the North Carolina site's reinspection, with a decision due in 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing. The incretin market is ≈$128B, down from ≈$135B, because US net prices fell ~15% on flat volume and ex-US generics deepened.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. MariTide's first-dose vomiting adds a new pattern: one dose cannot be skipped quickly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MariTide carries titration and first-dose counselling.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: On-drug delay of gastric emptying is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~55,000 filed and tolled claims. A second bellwether in Feb 2031 was a defence verdict, and settlement talks are ongoing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to add persistent gastroparesis. Reserves increased.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; absolute numbers stable.
No causal confirmation in longer data; low absolute risk; still inside the MDL.
Now concentrated among 9.3M users aged 65+ on the Medicare benefit, about half of whom complete only the one required counselling visit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label stands. The permanent Medicare benefit keeps a single counselling visit; no ongoing body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women; Medicare claims show rising absolute fracture counts as the 65+ user base grows.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended for 65+ and postmenopausal women. Pediatric bone-accrual study ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; very low absolute risk.

The 2031 retatrutide postmarketing study showed a dose-dependent anhedonia-scale shift, clinically meaningful in ~14% at the top dose. Whether it is a class effect is still argued; surveys hold at 10–15% of long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label adds 'reduced pleasure/anhedonia' to adverse reactions (Nov 2031). FTC consent orders with three focus-subscription brands (2031). No class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fewer structural stops under permanent public coverage, but regain remains the norm for those who stop.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No federal rule; Indiana waiver litigation ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D and protein signals persist in older and low-income users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult follow-up and nine in adolescents.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric growth velocity and pubertal timing (children started before 12)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: An interim analysis of the mandated liraglutide registry (~41,000 children aged 6–11) found height velocity 0.8–1.2 cm/yr below matched controls over two years, concentrated in children losing >10% of body weight, and later thelarche/gonadarche. Endocrinologists split on whether this is harm or a correction of obesity-advanced bone age and early puberty. Final adult-height data are not expected before the mid-2030s.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (May 2032). Liraglutide 6–11 label now requires quarterly height and Tanner staging. AAP limits under-12 initiation to pediatric endocrinologists. HRSA paused new 6–11 starts at FQHCs; continuing children are monitored.

safety_ledger.effect: Restrictive eating disorder in adolescents who started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A US–Danish claims cohort shows ARFID and anorexia diagnoses at HR ~1.6 in those who started before 14, highest after discontinuation. Confounding by obesity-related eating pathology is not excluded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Under FDA review; eating-disorder screening added to AAP guidance.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls have plateaued at roughly 2030 levels; dosing errors and impurity in research retatrutide persist.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts; first DOJ indictment of a research-peptide distributor (2032); no prosecution of users.

safety_ledger.effect: Prolonged adverse effects after monthly dosing (MariTide)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Long half-life means GI effects and any reaction cannot be stopped quickly; early pharmacovigilance reports of 3–4-week nausea runs.

food_and_beverage.state: With adoption flat at ~19%, snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes have stopped falling faster and now sit at a lower baseline. Guidance is rebased rather than cut. Medicaid opt-in states show the last leg of decline. Protein, fibre and 'bone' formats are mature categories, and senior nutrition lines grow with the Medicare benefit.

alcohol.state: AUD parity and HRSA provision keep reaching heavy drinkers. Spirits volume falls a further ~4%, and beer is flat to down. Premium low-volume and non-alcoholic lines grow. State excise forecasts now assume the lower base.

restaurants.state: Two-menu service and small plates are standard. Value-volume chains have finished their closures. Senior-heavy markets such as Maricopa County see early-bird traffic fall as the Medicare benefit lands.

apparel.state: Wide size runs and 'athletic cut' are baseline. Plus-size has stabilised at a smaller share, and adaptive clothing for older people losing weight grows.

fitness.state: Medicare Advantage plans bundle strength classes with the counselling visit. Low-cost gyms keep their subsidy users. The research-peptide gray market persists on gym floors.

insurance.state: Commercial pharmacy trend eases to ~+6% as retirees and low-wage workers shift to Medicare and Medicaid and cash prices fall. Employer weight coverage is down to 54%. Life insurers ask applicants who are off the drug why they stopped.

pharma.state: Volume is flat and net prices are down ~15%. Lilly leads, and Amgen enters with MariTide. Novo is stabilising but carries the MDL. Companies are planning for US semaglutide generics in 2033.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug is unremarkable; being off it invites a question. The finish still reads as class: muscle, bone and molecule. Among older people it now reads as Medicare.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 'Charlotte build' persists in finance. The new local story is Maricopa County's retirement communities. In Sun City and Mesa, women aged 65–80 on the $50-copay Medicare benefit made 'on' the default at the pickleball club, and the holdouts are asked whether they have had their counselling visit. The bone-density gap now runs between the women who do the strength classes and the women who don't.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Small plates and two menus are normal. Family doctors now ask about children's growth charts as well as portions. Some parents of 6–11-year-olds are taking them off liraglutide and eating differently at home.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Molecule disclosure on profiles is routine and less loaded. 'Monthly' is a new tag, and some read it as 'can't easily take a break'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still clinical, but 'the grey' is now an acknowledged cost. Choosing to keep appetite, or pleasure, is defensible if you explain it.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. 10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure; ~14% at top-dose retatrutide on a validated scale. Surveys find ~40% of users who have been on for more than two years have planned a dose reduction or 'flat-week' holiday. Focus subscriptions are down from 1.5–2M to ~0.9M after the FTC orders.
interior_life.framing: A side effect that is managed. Primary-care templates now ask 'Any flatness?' 'The grey' is a standard complaint, and holidays are prescribed. Monthly MariTide users can only change dose a month at a time.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employer-paid focus perks have been mostly withdrawn after the FTC orders and EEOC guidance on perks tied to medication. Sales and creative workers schedule flat-week holidays around pitches. DOT drivers still need tirzepatide or MariTide for apnea clearance. Union bans on employers viewing adherence data spread to two more contracts.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is no longer a selling point because so many artists take holidays; reviewers ask what dose an album was 'made at'. Sports-betting handle in high-uptake states has stabilised at a lower base.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists schedule holidays with couples. Monthly users plan anniversaries a month ahead, and some switch back to weekly to keep that control.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Coverage is bipartisan and popular among seniors. Candidates who are off are asked why. The pediatric growth signal gives 'natural-body' activists their first clinical argument, and HRSA's renewal debate now includes children's height charts.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access on payment and defensive on safety: no new indications, a Drug Safety Communication on pediatric growth, a retatrutide anhedonia label, CRL caution on survodutide and amycretin, and MariTide approved with a postmarketing study.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Permanent Medicare Part D obesity benefit ($245/$50) from Jan 2032; CMS Medicaid National Incretin Rate ($199) with 36 states plus DC opted in; HRSA programme on a two-year $4.8B appropriation. No mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Indiana and Arkansas waivers keep the 80% PDC rule and quarterly weigh-ins. Indiana now counts clinic-given monthly MariTide toward PDC and steers members to it. National-rate states may not add weigh-ins without a waiver. HRSA asks only for refill pickup, plus quarterly height checks for children.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea screening is unchanged. The Army recruit policy is unchanged. The VA adds MariTide to its formulary for veterans with obesity.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs remain, with exemptions granted in exchange for the price agreement. Indian API still feeds 503A compounders and mail pens, and the 2033 US generic entry has started Indian–US manufacturing deals.

events.event: Retatrutide postmarketing study reports dose-dependent anhedonia-scale shifts, clinically meaningful in ~14% at the top dose; FDA adds 'reduced pleasure' to the label in November and the FTC signs consent orders with three 'focus' subscription brands

Administration and manufacturers announce a price agreement tied to tariff exemptions: TrumpRx cash falls to $249 for semaglutide, $299 for tirzepatide and $149 for oral starting doses; Medicare's negotiated payment drops to $245
FDA approves Amgen's MariTide, a monthly injection, for chronic weight management at $1,100 list and $299 cash, with a postmarketing study on prolonged adverse effects

Year-end spending package makes the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge a permanent Part D obesity benefit from January 2032, keeping the $50 copay and the 65+ counselling visit, and gives the HRSA Community Incretin Access Program a two-year $4.8B appropriation
CMS sets a $199 Medicaid National Incretin Rate for states that cover obesity; 36 states and DC opt in by year's end, and public programmes overtake commercial plans in incretin fills

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication after the pediatric liraglutide registry shows slower height growth and later puberty in children started at 6–11; HRSA pauses new under-12 starts at health centres

open_tensions: The pediatric growth signal is ambiguous. It could be harm, or a correction of obesity-advanced growth and puberty, and adult-height data are years away. About 60,000 children aged 6–11 stay on the drug under quarterly measurement, while HRSA's pause leaves new low-income families without the free option that affluent families can still buy through private endocrinologists.

Public programmes are now the default payer and are locked into $245 and $199 branded rates just as US semaglutide generics are due in 2033. Most of the public spend buys low-monitoring regimens for the 65+ and low-income users the bone and muscle labels warn about.

Normalisation and complaint pull against each other. Being off needs explaining, but 'the grey' is now a recognised cost. Monthly dosing, which Indiana is steering Medicaid members toward, makes it harder to take a holiday just as holidays have become standard practice.
The 8.5M gray-market users and the ~55,000-claim MDL both remain unresolved. A global settlement could reshape labels before the pancreatitis and gastroparesis science settles.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Off It? You'll Have to Explain: Medicare Now Pays for America's Weight Drugs, and Its Children Are Being Measured
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2032 the number of Americans on an incretin drug has barely moved, about 19 in every 100 adults or fifty-two million people. What has changed is who pays. Public programmes now buy more of these drugs than every employer plan combined.

A year-end spending bill in December 2031 made Medicare's temporary obesity bridge a permanent benefit. The copay is still fifty dollars, and Medicare now pays a negotiated $245 a month instead of $275. In February, Medicaid set a national rate of $199, and thirty-six states and Washington DC have signed on. The federal programme that hands out free generic liraglutide at community health centres, and free semaglutide for quitting smoking and drinking, was funded for two years at $4.8 billion. Branded cash prices fell under a deal with manufacturers: $249 for semaglutide, $299 for tirzepatide, $149 for a starter pill. List prices still exist, and almost nobody pays them. Wegovy still lists at $1,349 and retatrutide at $1,499, and retatrutide is still rationed. Nine million gray-market users have shrunk to eight and a half, because the price gap is smaller and the habit stays.

In the retirement towns around Phoenix, the Medicare benefit made the drug the default. In Sun City, a woman of seventy who isn't on it gets asked whether she has had her counselling visit yet. The counselling visit is one appointment, and the strength classes the Medicare Advantage plans bundle with it are optional. Fracture counts are rising slowly in Medicare claims, roughly in line with the 2028 label's warning.

The first monthly injection arrived in September 2031. Amgen's MariTide is a shot given once a month, sometimes by a nurse. Indiana's Medicaid programme, which still checks refill records and weighs its members every quarter, now steers them toward it, because a shot given in a clinic counts automatically as taking the drug. For the first time, staying on is something that happens to you unless you act.

That matters because the dulling of pleasure is now an accepted complaint rather than something you could buy. A large postmarketing study of retatrutide in 2031 found a dose-dependent drop in pleasure scores, and the label now says so. The Federal Trade Commission ended the 'focus' subscription business's mood claims, and employers quietly dropped the perk. 'The grey' is now a question on the primary-care intake form. About four in ten long-term users have planned a lighter week or a break, around pitches, anniversaries or a holiday dinner. People on the monthly shot have to plan a month ahead, and some have switched back to weekly to keep control.

The children are the part that is unsettled. A registry required when liraglutide was approved for six-to-eleven-year-olds reported in May that the children it tracks grew about a centimetre less per year than similar children not on the drug, and entered puberty later. Half of pediatric endocrinology says this is harm. The other half says children with obesity grow fast and mature early, and this may be the body coming back toward normal. Adult heights will not be known for years. The FDA issued a safety communication, the label now requires quarterly height checks, and the federal clinics stopped starting new children under twelve. About sixty thousand stay on. Parents who can pay for a private pediatric endocrinologist can still start their children.

Food companies have rebased their sales targets rather than cut them again. Spirits volumes keep falling. The gastroparesis lawsuits sit at fifty-five thousand claims while settlement talks continue. Generic semaglutide is due in 2033. From a distance the country looks steady. The drug has become as routine as statins, and the people who are not on it now have to explain why.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tamika Reyes clocks out of a home-care visit in Merrillville at 11:40 and drives to the health centre on Broadway, because Marcus's appointment is at noon and they measure height before lunch now.

Marcus is ten. He takes off his shoes without being asked. The nurse lowers the bar onto his hair, reads it, and types. On the screen his line has gone from steep to gentle. The nurse says it's within the range they discussed. She hands Tamika the same blue sheet as last quarter, with the pen refills stapled to it.

'Can I ask him something?' the doctor says, and asks Marcus whether he ever skips lunch on purpose. Marcus says the cafeteria pizza is gross. Everyone laughs a little.

In the car Tamika eats half a turkey wrap and saves the rest. Her own shot is Thursday. Next quarter she's supposed to move to the monthly one at the Medicaid clinic, which means no more refill-count letters and no more choosing, and she hasn't decided how she feels about that.

At four she stands on the kiosk at the pharmacy, scans her card, and waits for the green check. It comes.

At dinner her sister calls about Thanksgiving and asks whether Marcus will eat, whether Tamika is doing her week off. 'Maybe,' Tamika says. 'I'd like to taste the dressing.'

After Marcus is asleep she opens the growth chart app and slides the line with her finger, forward a year, two years, to where the dotted line stops.
